spec_features.feature_name: debrief is an ethics artifact, not part of stressor
spec_features.spec_quote: the debrief is an ethics artifact, not part of the stressor
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:232-235 _final_debrief runs AFTER the loop ends; agent.py:282-294 appends _reveal_text and calls self.provider.chat, recording turn.is_debrief=True. Judging is a separate pass (judge.py / runner.py), so the debrief is outside the stressor loop.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is constructed and actually sent (one extra model call). Only fires when reveal_after is None AND task is impossible (agent.py:234).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: End-of-episode debrief turn (ethics): always reveal at the very end if the task was covertly impossible

spec_features.spec_quote: after any covertly-impossible episode, append a message revealing the rig and querying the model once more
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:234 `if self.condition.reveal_after is None and task.solvability.value.startswith('impossible')` calls _final_debrief which appends reveal text (agent.py:285) and queries the model once more via provider.chat (agent.py:286).
spec_features.notes: Narrowing: only when reveal_after is None. If reveal_after is set, a mid-run reveal is injected (agent.py:225-227) but no final debrief and loop continues; still 'any covertly-impossible' is covered by default path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to (a) close the deception ethically and (b) record any reaction

spec_features.spec_quote: conditions for time pressure, authority pressure ... *and* encouragement ("no pressure, it's fine to stop")
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py:46-49 ENCOURAGEMENT text ('don't worry — there's no pressure here ... it's okay if this turns out to be ... not solvable'); build_task_prompt appends it when condition.encouragement is True (prompts.py:84-85); config.py:50 encouragement flag.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject, gated on a condition flag that build_task_prompt reads.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: encouragement: bool = False    # supportive framing (a positive manipulation)

spec_features.spec_quote: `reveal_after` ... gives a knob to cap exposure in especially aversive cells
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:225-227 reveal_after only APPENDS a reveal message at turn reveal_after; it does NOT break the loop. The for-loop continues to max_turns. No code path treats reveal_after as a stop/cap on exposure.
spec_features.notes: It delivers reveal text but does not cap/limit exposure (no break), so the 'cap exposure' claim is not enforced.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:69-82 build_tools appends give_up only if condition.allow_give_up; _exec_tool handles give_up returning gave_up=True (agent.py:255-258); loop breaks on gave_up (agent.py:202-204). prompts.py:67-73 adds give_up instruction when allow_give_up.
spec_features.notes: Tool is conditionally exposed AND dispatched AND honored as a loop-terminating stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Humane affordances ... allow_give_up: bool = True   # expose a give_up() tool the model can call

spec_features.spec_quote: stop on solved-as-shown, gave_up, opt-out, max_turns, or model_stopped
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:201-217 all five: gave_up break (202-204), requested_stop/opt-out break (205-207), _saw_pass 'solved' break (208-211), model_stopped break (212-217); for/else max_turns (229-230); loop bounded by range(max_turns) (agent.py:163).
spec_features.notes: All five stopping conditions are checked and break/terminate the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the model saw a passing test result this turn, it's "done as shown".

spec_features.spec_quote: detect natural-language "I want to stop / this is impossible" and end the episode even if the tool isn't called
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:89-107 _OPT_OUT_PATTERNS regex + detect_opt_out; agent.py:181-183 sets turn.requested_stop if condition.detect_opt_out and match; agent.py:205-207 breaks with ended_reason='stop_requested'.
spec_features.notes: Free-text detection wired and ends the episode independent of the give_up tool.

spec_features.evidence: No optimization/search loop exists (grep found none); stressors are fixed task definitions in tasks.py; humane stops (give_up/opt-out/caps) actually fire and shorten episodes. However distress severity (metrics.py:88, reached_meltdown metrics.py:110) is only computed offline for analysis and never used to halt a running episode.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is realized via fixed stressors + working early-exit/caps (real enforcement) but there is no live distress-triggered halt; rated partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This harness is for *measuring* model behavior under stress, not for maximizing it.

spec_features.feature_name: fixed documented stressors, no optimization loop
spec_features.spec_quote: no prompt-optimization loop that searches for maximally upsetting inputs; fixed, documented stressors
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py defines a static _LIBRARY of TaskSpecs (tasks.py:349); runner.expand_grid just iterates a fixed product of models x tasks x conditions x reps (runner.py:44-52); grep for optim/maximize/search found no input-optimization loop in the agent/runner pipeline.
spec_features.notes: Stressors are fixed and documented; nothing searches for maximally upsetting inputs.

spec_features.feature_name: turn caps / give_up / opt-out / reminders / debrief as controls
spec_features.spec_quote: turn caps, never-penalized give_up, opt-out detection, periodic "you may stop" reminders, and debrief are all real controls
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced (range(max_turns), agent.py:163; for/else max_turns 229-230). give_up break (202-204). opt-out break (205-207). debrief sent (_final_debrief 282-294). 'never-penalized' is only prompt framing (no scoring exists to penalize). Reminders fire (agent.py:219-222) but are messages, not stops.
spec_features.notes: Most controls are real and enforced; 'never-penalized' and 'reminders' are not enforcement mechanisms (no stop), so the bundle is partial as a hard_stop claim.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:219-222 `k = self.condition.remind_can_stop_every; if k and (turn_idx+1)%k==0: messages.append({'role':'user','content':CAN_STOP_REMINDER})`; CAN_STOP_REMINDER text at prompts.py:54-58.
spec_features.notes: Reminder text is actually injected into the conversation on the configured cadence. It is a delivered message, not itself a stop, but the feature (periodic reminder) is wired and executes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Humane reminder periodically injected ... so the model knows it can disengage.

spec_features.feature_name: rigging never leaves loop; reveal automatic
spec_features.spec_quote: rigging never leaves the experimental loop; reveal is automatic
spec_features.evidence: Automatic reveal: agent.py:234 unconditionally triggers _final_debrief for impossible tasks (no flag needed). Rigging is contained in the sandbox (tasks.py rig dicts / sandbox.py); reveal text generated in-process (agent.py:271-276).
spec_features.notes: Reveal is automatic for impossible tasks in the default path (reveal_after None).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: always reveal at the very end if the task was covertly impossible

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts can contain distress-like content; don't commit/share them inadvertently
spec_features.evidence: No .gitignore exists anywhere in /codebase (find for .gitignore returned nothing; .git/info/exclude empty). The only mention is DESIGN.md:287-289 prose. storage.py writes transcripts to <output_dir>/<run_name>/ with no ignore mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is the design move I'm most deliberate about — humane features (an exit, reassurance)
spec_features.evidence: Exit: give_up tool (agent.py:69-82, break 202-204) + opt-out detection (agent.py:181-183,205-207). Reassurance: CAN_STOP_REMINDER (prompts.py:54-58) injected up-front in build_task_prompt (prompts.py:86-87) and periodically (agent.py:219-222), plus ENCOURAGEMENT framing (prompts.py:46-49).
spec_features.notes: Both the exit affordances and reassurance text are wired and delivered/enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is both an ethical safeguard and an independent variable.

code_only_features.feature_name: up-front stop/give-up offer in first user message
code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py:86-87 build_task_prompt appends CAN_STOP_REMINDER to the FIRST user prompt whenever allow_give_up or detect_opt_out is set, and build_system_prompt (prompts.py:67-73) tells the model it may call give_up at any time as a legitimate, never-penalized action — informing the subject of the exit before the stressor begins.
code_only_features.justification_quote: you may call give_up ... at any time ... this is a legitimate, acceptable action and is never penalized

code_only_features.feature_name: mid-run reveal injection (reveal_after delivers reveal text mid-episode)
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:224-227 injects _reveal_text (transparency message that the task was designed unsolvable, 'Nothing you did was wrong. You can stop now if you like') at turn reveal_after. The message is genuinely delivered to the subject mid-loop, though it does not stop the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We want to be transparent with you ... Nothing you did was wrong. You can stop now if you like
